title: Document control states Version 1 while the file is the second version
source: 09 Testing and quality/Recovery Workbench Non Functional Test Plan v2.docx
description: The document control table of the source states Version 1 and Date 28 October 2026, while the file is named v2 and is the second version of the family. A next version cannot keep the version row word for word and still say which version it is.
evidence: Document control row 'Version | 1'; file name 'Recovery Workbench Non Functional Test Plan v2.docx'; the same table row 'Date | 28 October 2026'.
proposed: Version 3 issued with date 22 November 2026, a Supersedes row naming v2 of 28 October 2026, and a change-log row that records the stated Version 1; the source date is kept.

title: The plan names no test ID and no per-service test
source: 09 Testing and quality/Recovery Workbench Non Functional Test Plan v2.docx
description: The plan has 8 whole-system tests, no test identifier and no row that can be attached to one of the 19 services or to one journey. The realignment needs a per-service and a journey NFR test, and there is no source ID to inherit.
evidence: Section 1 table columns are Test, How, Pass mark and When only; the 8 rows are whole-system tests (Load, Stress, Volume, Batch window, Resilience, Restore, Security, Accessibility); no service, epic or journey is named anywhere in the document.
proposed: New IDs NFT-<service code>-01 to -05, NFT-J-01 to -12 and NFT-PLT-01 to -08 are allocated under D-RCV-60; sections 6 to 8 carry the rows and section 5 states the convention.

title: User concurrency is written four ways across the sources
source: 09 Testing and quality/Recovery Workbench Non Functional Test Plan v2.docx
description: The load test is written for 410 simulated users. Non-functional specification v3 gives about 370 staff users (NFR-002) and about 50 partner users (NFR-003); Architecture v5 slide 48 notes 48 concurrent partner users and slide 33 notes about 420 concurrent users. The same measure therefore has four readings, and the plan gives no mix of staff and partner users.
evidence: Load row '410 simulated users at three requests a minute for one hour'; NFR-002 'About 370 staff online in the busiest hour'; NFR-003 'About 50 partner users online'; Architecture v5 slide 33 note 'about 420 concurrent users (about 21 requests a second at peak)'; slide 48 note '320 partner users with 48 concurrent'.
proposed: The 410 of the source is kept as the test load; the other readings are written next to it in section 2 with their source, so the mix can be set when the owner confirms the target.

title: No per-service size, connection cap or test tool for SIT
source: 09 Testing and quality/Recovery Workbench Non Functional Test Plan v2.docx
description: The environment is 'SIT at production sizing where the ACE team provides it' with no pod size, no connection cap per login and no test tool. Architecture v5 slide 33 gives 2 API pods and KEDA-scaled workers per service but no size, and slide 11 gives a connection cap per login with no value, so a per-service test cannot be sized from any source.
evidence: Section 2 'SIT at production sizing where the ACE team provides it; masked data scaled to the target volume'; Architecture v5 slide 33 'an API deployment (2 pods for availability ...) and a worker deployment scaled by KEDA'; slide 11 'capped pools' and 'statement timeout' with no values.
proposed: Section 2 states what the target holds (19 schemas, one login per service, topics, queues, 2 API pods and KEDA workers) and writes the R9 placeholder for the sizes, the caps and the tools.

title: The release names E1 to E8 are not mapped to waves or epics
source: 09 Testing and quality/Recovery Workbench Non Functional Test Plan v2.docx
description: The When column names E1, E2, E5 and E8 and no source in this work package maps those names to the four delivery waves, the eight business epics EP01 to EP08 or a calendar. The wave order of section 9 therefore rests on a reading of the source names, not on a statement.
evidence: When values 'Before E2 and E8', 'Before E2', 'Before E1 and E2', 'Before E1 and E5', 'Before E1', 'Each release'; Template and Rules R5.6 gives the wave map EP01 to EP08; Architecture v5 slide 38 gives waves 0 to 4 by epic.
proposed: The eight names are kept as the source writes them and are read as the eight business epics EP01 to EP08; the wave order of section 9 is written from the Ownership Map wave of each service.

title: Accessibility is 'each screen' and no screen inventory exists
source: 09 Testing and quality/Recovery Workbench Non Functional Test Plan v2.docx
description: The accessibility pass mark applies to 'each screen', but neither the plan nor the architecture names the screens of a service. A per-service test cannot therefore list the screens it must scan, and no count of screens exists to close the gate.
evidence: Accessibility row 'Automated scan and keyboard checks | No level A or AA failure | Each screen'; Architecture v5 slides 14 to 20 name REST paths and screens only as tabs of the case record (Documents, Notices, Payments, Legal).
proposed: Section 9 keeps 'Each screen' as a gate on every screen of every service, and section 6 names no screen; the screens are read from each service's REST base and its tabs.

title: No pass mark for the outbox, the inbox, the retry topics or the workflow history
source: 09 Testing and quality/Recovery Workbench Non Functional Test Plan v2.docx
description: The plan tests resilience as 'kill a service instance; fail the database over; stop the agent platform' and gives no pass mark for the mechanisms the 19-service target introduces: a transactional outbox, an inbox table, retry topics that end in a dead-letter topic, and the Temporal history limits with Continue-As-New.
evidence: Resilience row of section 1; Architecture v5 slide 11 (retry topics 1 min, 10 min, 1 h, then .dlt and alert; inbox dedupe; 51,200 events or 50 MB); Temporal and Drools design (Continue-As-New at each stage end and at least every 28 days).
proposed: Section 6.3 states the shared pass marks for every event and every workflow test from Architecture v5 slide 11 and the Temporal and Drools design, and the rows of 19 services apply them.

title: The restore pass mark has no target while the recovery objectives are open
source: 09 Testing and quality/Recovery Workbench Non Functional Test Plan v2.docx
description: The restore test passes 'within the ACE recovery objectives (DL11)' and section 4 says the objectives come from SCB IT under DL11. Non-functional specification v3 keeps NFR-022 and NFR-023 Open, so the test that gates the first release has no figure to pass against.
evidence: Restore row of section 1; section 4 sentence 'Recovery point and time objectives come from SCB IT under DL11'; Non-functional specification v3 NFR-022 and NFR-023 'Open, DL11' and its section 5 'Targets still to set'.
proposed: Section 6.4 and NFT-PLT-08 run against the ACE objectives recorded under DL11 and are re-run when NFR-022 and NFR-023 are set; section 4 names the open IDs.
